text:
Eeli Tolvanen is in his first season with the Rangers after his years in Seattle, playing about 12 minutes a night on the third line. He has four goals and six points in 23 games, and the goals are right on his expected total.

The Rangers have been leaning on him for energy more than offense: 39 hits and 21 blocked shots. The on-ice numbers are rough. New York gets 47% of the expected goals with him on at five on five, about eight points worse than when he sits, and Evolving-Hockey had a similar story last season, though he played with some of the weakest teammates in the league.

The shot is still the tool. NHL Edge has his hardest at the 88th percentile among forwards, and he's scoring on 16.7% of his shots, above his range, so the goals may slow before they speed up.

What to watch: whether he can push into a bigger role. His ice time has swung between about 6 and 13 minutes over the last ten games, which is the coaching staff telling you it's still deciding.
